summary: A 1913 Conservation Commission station on Tooley Pond Mountain whose steel tower was taken down in 1971 and rebuilt on Cathedral Rock by Ranger School students.

access.note: The register says it can be visited by the Latham Trail from the NYS Ranger School campus. No closure notice found; check with the school before going.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia's lead dates first construction on Tooley Pond to 1919, but its History section and the 1913 Conservation Commission report describe a wooden station in 1913, with the steel tower following in 1919.

The register's late-1990s re-erection and Wikipedia's 1980s start with a 1999 cab finish and 2000 completion are not fully reconciled; the 1982 newspaper shows erection under way by then, so the work spanned both decades.

sources.title: Hikes, climbs along historic Tooley Pond Road

notes_for_editor: Dates for the move are the weakest part. The register says late 1990s; Wikipedia says the rebuild began in the 1980s, the cab was finished in 1999 and the tower was dedicated in July 2000; a 1982 newspaper shows erection under way. Wikipedia cites a 2021 Adirondack Mountain Club book and a NYSFFLA list that were not checked. The 1971 removal rests on Wikipedia alone. The 47-foot height is given without a cab-floor figure, so height_m is left out. The record's 'relocated' event had no year; 1982 is the first dated mention, not the move date. The sister record us-ny-tooley-pond-mountain carries an unverified location (44.27104, -74.93038) that these sources do not confirm. Current access is unverified beyond the register's wording. The Adirondack Explorer hike write-up (cite 5) also dates the reassembly to 2000; the story does not give that date.
